profiles.summary: The interpreter revision behind reth v2.10.1, the last unread Ethereum backend on the Pocket gateway, was read and run. Its arithmetic, shift, comparison, jump and jump destination code equals the v2.11.0 revision except for one equivalent SIGNEXTEND index read and one extra length check on RETURN and REVERT, and the battery, the targeted set and 14,598 new edge vectors give the specified word on every call pinned to it. Two single-build public endpoints (reth v2.10.0 and geth v1.17.9) can now stand in for the challenged reference endpoint and give the stored reference words on the battery, the targeted set and script set 1.

deltas.delta: reth v2.10.1 differs from v2.10.0 only in the evm2 interpreter revision: v2.10.0 pins DaniPopes/evm2 592bf18c4e22fff54ac9b4db606c4ee276e345cb and v2.10.1 pins alloy-rs/evm2 01df8f6a396d0250da286cb763faa6ec292d65b5. Both pin ruint 1.21.1. v2.11.0 pins DaniPopes/evm2 66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475.

At evm2 01df8f6a the files i256.rs (signed division and remainder), bytecode/analysis/x86.rs, bytecode/analysis/aarch64.rs, interpreter/memory.rs and storage_key.rs are byte identical to 66687c18. arithmetic.rs differs in one line: SIGNEXTEND reads the low limb of the index (as_limbs()[0]) where 66687c18 calls wrapping_to::<u64>(), and both sit behind a test of the whole word against 31, so the bit index is the same. bitwise.rs, memory.rs and the instruction module differ only in tests and in where require_non_staticcall is defined. control.rs has one extra check: RETURN and REVERT fail with MemoryLimitOOG when offset plus length exceeds 2^32, where 66687c18 leaves that to the memory resize, which fails on gas long before; JUMP and JUMPI are the same (whole-word condition, saturated target, bitmap lookup).

evm2 01df8f6a adds zero-copy call input: without an inspector, a CALL child reads its calldata straight from the caller frame's memory (Interpreter::call_input with lends_memory set in run_interpreter), and copies it as soon as an inspector hook runs. Each frame has its own memory vector, and the caller is suspended while the child runs. This is the only change from 592bf18c (reth v2.10.0) in the interpreter, and it is the path every hook call (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134) and every token transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:73) of the PoolManager takes on that build. v2.11.0 replaces the raw borrowed slice with a range into the caller's memory.

The evm2 compiler stage at 01df8f6a has the same SIGNEXTEND constant fold as 66687c18 (low limb behind a whole-word test), falls back to the generic path for EXP with a constant exponent, and its CREATE builtin sets code_address to the caller where 66687c18 sets the destination. reth v2.10.1 builds the compiler in by default and leaves it off (--jit defaults to false), as v2.11.0 does.

Single-build public endpoints that accept eth_call with state overrides on 2026-11-26: eth-mainnet.public.blastapi.io (reth/v2.10.0-f5192ac, 20 of 20 version reads, eth_call gas cap about 550 million), ethereum.public.blockpi.network (Geth/v1.17.9-stable-9dffe6e9 go1.27.2, 20 of 20, about 600 million), public-eth.nownodes.io (Geth/v1.17.10 go1.27.3, 20 of 20, 50 million), eth.blockrazor.xyz (Geth/v1.17.5 go1.25.12) and eth.rpc.blxrbdn.com (Geth/v1.16.7 go1.25.14). eth-pokt.nodies.app (reth/v2.7.0) answered 20 of 20 version reads and then refused eth_call with HTTP 403. rpc.flashbots.net rotates reth v2.6.0 and v2.10.0 and refuses eth_call with overrides. ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com still answers with a challenge page.

deltas.delta: erigon v3.8.2, which answers some Pocket gateway calls, changes no file of execution/vm against v3.8.1 and keeps holiman/uint256 at v1.3.3-0.20260228135838-087f4b32f234. Its state changes fix two faults of the default parallel executor (exec.workers defaults to half the CPU count): HasSelfdestructed reported a self-destruct by an earlier transaction of the block as one of the current transaction, and touched empty accounts were not removed through the version map.

.NET 10 reports Vector512.IsHardwareAccelerated false by default on Intel family 6 model 0x55 (Skylake server, Cascade Lake, Cooper Lake) and on Cannon Lake, by capping the preferred vector width at 256 bits. On those CPUs Nethermind's jump destination analysis takes the Vector256 kernel. Ice Lake server and later Intel parts and AMD Zen 4 and Zen 5 have AVX-512 VBMI and no cap, so they take the Vector512 kernel.

profiles.summary: Transient storage on reth v2.10.1 behaves as on v2.11.0: the journal entries, the rollback and the clear at the end of a transaction were read, and sequence c2 (a hook writes slot0 between the lock check and the swap's read) returns the reference words on calls pinned to reth v2.10.1 and to erigon v3.8.1.

deltas.delta: evm2 01df8f6a stores transient storage in one map keyed by address and slot, journals every effective TSTORE with the previous value, removes zero entries, restores them on rollback and clears the whole map in clear_transaction_state. The isolated-state helpers that differ from 66687c18 are compiled for tests only.

cleared.result: No arithmetic, shift, comparison, jump or analysis path differs in behaviour. i256.rs, both analysis kernels, interpreter memory and storage_key.rs are byte identical. The SIGNEXTEND index is read from the low limb behind a whole-word test against 31 (arithmetic.rs lines 57-63), so TickMath.sol:61, TickBitmap.sol:20-21, 38, 54-55, Slot0.sol:49, BalanceDelta.sol:25-41 and 69, LiquidityMath.sol:12 and Pool.sol:576 get the specified word. The extra RETURN and REVERT bound fails only past 2^32 bytes, which no PoolManager return reaches. The DUPN, SWAPN and EXCHANGE helpers differ, and the PoolManager bytecode has none of their bytes at an instruction boundary. ruint is 1.21.1 in both builds.

cleared.check: Zero-copy call input of evm2 01df8f6a: can the callee's calldata change or dangle while it is read, so that a hook or token sees other bytes than the PoolManager wrote?
cleared.result: No, as read. The borrowed slice points into the caller frame's own memory vector (Memory holds one Vec per frame, interpreter/memory.rs lines 6-10), the caller is suspended until the child returns, a reentrant PoolManager frame gets its own memory, Clone and to_bytes copy the bytes so a kept input owns them (message.rs lines 212-236), and Evm copies the input before any inspector hook can reach it (evm/mod.rs lines 1306-1308). The pinned runs above exercise it.

cleared.check: erigon v3.8.2 parallel executor fixes (a self-destruct of an earlier transaction read as the current one's, touched empty accounts not removed): does either reach PoolManager state on erigon v3.8.1 nodes?
cleared.result: No. HasSelfdestructed is read only by SELFDESTRUCT gas and refund code (execution/vm/gas_table.go line 781, operations_acl.go line 303), and the PoolManager bytecode has no SELFDESTRUCT (ASSUMPTIONS.md A10). The empty-account rule has nothing to remove on mainnet, where EIP-7523 records that no empty accounts exist, so a zero-value native take to an empty address (Currency.sol:48) touches nothing that is deleted. A block on which v3.8.1 differs would fork those nodes; that is a client fault, not a path to pool funds.

leads.question: Does erigon 3.8.2 (go1.27.4 and go1.27.2 builds behind the Pocket gateway) return the reference words for sequences c and c2 and the battery on calls pinned to it?

leadResults.answer: evm2 01df8f6a, which reth v2.10.1 pins and which is the only change from v2.10.0, has the same arithmetic, signed, shift, comparison, jump and jump destination code as 66687c18 apart from an equivalent SIGNEXTEND index read and an extra 2^32 bound on RETURN and REVERT. It adds zero-copy call input, which keeps the calldata in the suspended caller's own memory. On calls pinned to reth/v2.10.1-58ebce1 before and after, all 185,529 battery and targeted vectors, 14,598 new edge vectors, all 300 scripts of set 2 and 3 runs of sequence c2 gave the reference words. Correction from the cycle 27 critic: eth.api.pocket.network routes every request on its own (11 of 12 three-element web3_clientVersion batches mixed builds on 2026-11-26), so a read before and a read after do not show which backend ran the call between them. Every backend in the pool (reth v2.10.1, reth v2.11.0, erigon 3.8.1 and 3.8.2, geth v1.17.9) gave the specified words, but no vector is shown to have run on reth v2.10.1 alone.

eth-mainnet.public.blastapi.io (reth v2.10.0, about 550 million gas) and ethereum.public.blockpi.network (geth v1.17.9 go1.27.2, about 600 million gas) each name one build, accept state overrides, and gave the specified words for the battery, the targeted set and the new edge set and the stored reference for script set 1; blastapi also for set 2. Either can replace ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com in networks.json, with nownodes (geth v1.17.10, 50 million gas) as a second client.

Sequence c2 returned all 32 reference words on 2 calls pinned to erigon/3.8.1-cf6f1413 on both sides, and sequence c matched on 1 pinned call. Correction from the cycle 27 critic: eth.api.pocket.network routes every request on its own (11 of 12 three-element web3_clientVersion batches mixed builds on 2026-11-26), so a read before and a read after do not show which backend ran the call between them. Every backend in the pool (reth v2.10.1, reth v2.11.0, erigon 3.8.1 and 3.8.2, geth v1.17.9) gave the specified words, but no vector is shown to have run on reth v2.10.1 alone.

The kernel choice is now known: .NET 10 caps the vector width at 256 bits on Skylake server, Cascade Lake, Cooper Lake and Cannon Lake (codeman.cpp lines 1467-1508), so those CPUs take the Vector256 kernel, and Ice Lake server or later and Zen 4 or Zen 5 take the Vector512 VBMI kernel. The JIT's lowering of the intrinsics was not inspected, because no .NET runtime is available here. A lowering fault could only fork Nethermind nodes on one CPU family; it moves no funds.
No ruint release after 1.21.1 exists on the crates.io index as of 2026-11-26, so there is nothing to test yet; the question is carried as a new low lead with the 14,598 added vectors.

Hook question, answered in one line: the chain_id of a 7702 authorization is visible only in the type 4 transaction, no endpoint used here indexes transactions by authority, and cycle 23 already found no pool naming these addresses on a network where they are empty.

Not searched this cycle. collectProtocolFees and setProtocolFee need the fee controller (ProtocolFees.sol:36 and 48), so only clear and burn are open to an ordinary caller, and both already return the reference words through eth_call in script sets 1 and 2; the eth_getLogs probe for ProtocolFeeUpdated was refused by every endpoint for the full range.
